About the Position

Focusing on developing mixed-precision algorithms for numerical linear algebra on next-generation exascale supercomputers as part of the School of Computer Science Scholarship.

Application Deadline30 September 2026 at 05:00 UTC+5
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Basic Information

  • Project Title: Mixed Precision Methods for Numerical Linear Algebra at Exascale
  • Host Institution: University of Leeds
  • School/Faculty: School of Computer Science
  • Disciplines: Computer Science, Mathematics
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 05:00 UTC+5
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded
  • Eligibility: Worldwide (open to international and UK applicants)
  • Location: Leeds, United Kingdom
  • IELTS Required: Yes

Research Position Overview

This studentship is part of the School of Computer Science Scholarship 2025/26. It focuses on developing mixed-precision algorithms for numerical linear algebra on next-generation exascale supercomputers.

Research Context

Exascale computing requires exploiting multiple precision levels to balance accuracy and performance. Mixed-precision methods can dramatically speed up large-scale simulations.

What You Will Do

You will design and implement novel mixed-precision linear algebra routines, test them on state-of-the-art HPC systems, and analyse their numerical stability and efficiency.

Key Research Aims

  • Develop efficient mixed-precision algorithms for common linear algebra operations.
  • Evaluate performance and accuracy trade-offs on exascale architectures.
  • Contribute to open-source scientific software libraries.

Supervisor Profile

Supervisor not specified; check the School of Computer Science for potential advisors.

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Academic Background: First-class or 2:1 Honours degree in computer science, mathematics, or a related field.
  • English Language: IELTS required.
  • Nationality: Worldwide (no UK-only restriction).

Funding Details

  • Funding Type: School of Computer Science Scholarship.
  • Stipend: £21,805 per year.
  • Duration: 3.5 years.
  • Fees: Full academic fees covered (both UK and international fee rates).

How to Apply

Apply online via the University of Leeds PhD application portal.

Official Link

https://phd.leeds.ac.uk/project/2310-mixed-precision-methods-for-numerical-

  • Always confirm the full requirements and current deadline on the official website before applying.
  • Prepare the requested documents early — competitive awards are often decided on complete, on-time submissions.
